audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.40%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.52%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.63%, il VIX è sceso dello 2.05% sotto quota 20. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4780 dollari l'oncia con un rialzo dell'1.75%, mentre il petrolio è sceso del 5.24% a 93.32 dollari. Il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0.16% a 98.25, l'EUR/USD è sceso dello 0.21% a 1.17.

La UK ha registrato un'accelerazione dell'inflazione al 3.3% a marzo, mentre la BCE ha dichiarato di avere il 'lusso' di aspettare con le rialzi dei tassi d'interesse. La Cina ha tagliato il prezzo della benzina per la prima volta quest'anno.

Oggi si attendono dati macro importanti, tra cui il PIL QoQ USA in uscita il 29 aprile. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi d'interesse invariati, con un tasso depositi al 2.00%. L'ultima inflazione PCE Core YoY USA è stata del 3.0%.

Gli ETF hanno registrato afflussi significativi con un ingresso di 238.4 milioni di dollari.'}, {'altcoins': "Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna il 2.97% arrivando a 2391 dollari, Solana sale del 2.50% a 87.93 dollari e BNB aumenta dell'1.33% a 642.66 dollari."}, {'sentiment': 'Il Fear & Greed Index è a 32, classificandosi in zona Fear.'}]

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, con particolare attenzione agli indici PMI e ai dati sull'inflazione. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

Asian markets closed mixed. The Nikkei gained 0.40% to 59,586, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.52% to 4106.26. These moves suggest a cautiously optimistic start for European markets.

In Western markets, the S&P 500 dropped 0.63% to 7064.01. The VIX fell 2.05% to 19.10, still below 20. The Dollar Index declined 0.16% to 98.25. Gold holds above $4780/oz, up 1.75%. Oil prices slid, with Brent crude down 5.24% to $93.32. The 10-year US yield rose to 4.29%, up 0.99%.

On the macro front, UK inflation accelerated to 3.3% in March, driven by rising petrol prices. The ECB is considering interest rate rises but has the 'luxury' to wait, according to a top policymaker. Additionally, China cut gasoline prices for the first time this year despite tensions with Iran.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is up two point three four percent, with a daily net inflow into BTC ETFs of two hundred thirty-eight point four million dollars. The price is now seventy-eight thousand one hundred fifty dollars. 

In the altcoin space, Ethereum is up two point nine seven percent to two thousand three hundred ninety-one dollars, Solana rose two point five zero percent to eighty-seven point nine three dollars, and BNB increased one point three three percent to six hundred forty-two point six six dollars.

The Fear & Greed Index is at thirty-two, still in fear territory. That's all for now in the crypto space.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. Has the ECB’s rationale for the digital euro evolved over time, from a response to tech…

articles.title: The Risky Geography of the Cloud
articles.snippet: Iran's recent drone strikes on Gulf states mark the first time commercial data centers have been targeted in an organized fashion. Europe, especially, should reflect on the assumptions underlying digital-infrastructure investments and deployments, because attacks on data centers in the Middle East can jeopardize its own economic security.

articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. articles.title: What the War Against Iran Means for the U.S.-South Korean Alliance
articles.snippet: South Korea’s security is no longer confined to the peninsula. That is the real lesson from the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz. And if decision-makers in Seoul didn’t understand this before, they surely understand this now.The U.S.-South Korean alliance was built to deter North Korea, defend South Korea, and stabilize Northeast Asia. That mission remains indispensable, but a serious disruption in the Strait of Hormuz now hits South Korea directly through energy imports, shipping, industrial production, and economic confidence. For Seoul, this is not someone else’s regional crisis — it is a direct test of South Korean national resilience. The post What the War Against Iran Means for the U.S.-South Korean Alliance appeared first on War on the Rocks .
